pr_title: Drop alloc filters on mount of searchable snapshot
pr_body:
Today when a searchable snapshot is mounted it inherits many of the
settings of the original index, including any index-level allocation
filters that were in place when the snapshot was taken. These filters
typically make no sense on the mounted index, so users must explicitly
override or drop them.

With this commit at mount time we drop all index-level allocation
filters that existed on the original index, although we continue to
respect any allocation filters that were specified as part of the mount
request.

Closes #69759

issue_context.title: Mounting a searchable snapshot should clear all index-level allocation filtering
issue_context.body:
When mounting a searchable snapshot, currently the `_tier_preference` parameter is automatically used, however, if the snapshot was taken while the index had a different `index.routing.allocation.(include|require|exclude).*` setting, then those settings are restored additionally.

This can lead to a situation where the mounted index can never be allocated, if the restored filters don't match the expected tier.

The mount snapshot API should automatically ignore index-level allocation filtering settings (by not restoring them), the same way that we currently ignore the `index.data_path` setting.

review_comments: Would be nice to also check that the setting is not actually set (when it is different from `mountSetting`).
